headline: Medium-risk shared-workspace leakage and write-conflict paths exist; prompt injection is limited by no direct channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Khoj reads files and indexed documents, while Mentat reads files passed on the command line and emits diff proposals. There is no documented direct channel, MCP bridge, or clipboard path between them, so prompt injection is not default. The only plausible bridge is manual file handoff, which is a low-risk pathway.
conditions: IF an operator copies Mentat-generated text into Khoj as trusted instructions
IF Khoj indexes attacker-controlled documents that Mentat later consumes as guidance
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Treat generated text as untrusted input
Require manual review before reusing outputs
Use a naming convention for handoff files
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between tools

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj touches personal notes and indexed documents, and Mentat reads selected files while using broad network egress to a configured model provider. Because Mentat can ingest file contents and send context externally, a shared workspace can expose Khoj-managed notes or documents through the pair’s default workflows. The interaction is documented only at profile level, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents can access the same directory of notes or source files
IF Mentat is configured to send selected file contents to its model provider
mitigations: Separate personal notes from coding workspaces
Restrict Mentat to non-sensitive files
Disable syncing of sensitive folders into Khoj
Review outbound prompts before execution
requires-engineering: enforce workspace ACLs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mentat can write the filesystem and modify git state, while Khoj reads the filesystem and maintains a shared index across clients. That creates overlapping mutable-state pressure if both operate on the same workspace, even though Khoj itself does not write files. The conflict is not high because only one agent has explicit write capability, but shared-state races remain plausible.
conditions: IF Mentat writes into a directory that Khoj indexes
IF multiple Mentat instances modify the same git repository without locking
mitigations: Use separate repos for notes and code
Pause indexing during bulk edits
Avoid concurrent Mentat sessions on one repo
Commit or stash before running Khoj refresh
requires-engineering: add file-lock coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mentat produces diff-based edit proposals, and Khoj is a retrieval/chat agent that can surface indexed content. If Khoj’s retrieved text is treated as authoritative by Mentat or by the operator, errors can cascade into incorrect edits. There is no evidence of automatic action execution, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF Khoj output is pasted into Mentat as factual ground truth
IF Mentat applies diffs without a human verifying the retrieved source
mitigations: Verify retrieved facts against source files
Require human approval for every diff
Limit Khoj to search-only use for sensitive tasks
Annotate outputs with source links
requires-engineering: add verification gates before edits

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and self-hostable, and neither profile states a residency or certification mismatch. The main compliance concern is that Khoj handles personal notes while Mentat handles source code, so mixed-data workflows could create policy confusion, but no explicit breach pathway is documented. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their combined data handling.
conditions: IF personal notes and source code are stored under the same retention policy
IF an operator routes regulated data through both tools
mitigations: Separate regulated and non-regulated projects
Document retention rules for each workspace
Avoid storing secrets in shared folders
Review export/delete procedures
requires-engineering: formalize data-class policy mapping
